messages:
lena: Heads-up — dependency scanner just flagged CVE-2025-0001 in protobuf 3.20.x that's pulled into our inference runtime images. Also seeing advisories for a FlashAttention kernel overflow (vendor advisory) and a sentencepiece parsing edge-case (0.1.96). Need quick triage and rollout plan across Hosted / Dedicated / Private. :warning:

mike: ok can you paste the affected image tags? I can run a quick local build to reproduce.

lena: runtime-gpu:2026-02-11 and vllm-worker:2026-02-10 are both showing the protobuf lib. FlashAttention is shipped as a kernel package in our wheel builds.

tara: vllm uses protobuf mainly for RPC marshaling, not model weights. FlashAttention kernel CVE looks like a bounds check when sequence length>8192 — improbable for us but possible in stress tests. sentencepiece is parsing -> malformed input could OOM.

josh: From infra side we need to know if key rotation / KMS rewraps are involved when pushing rebuilt images to Dedicated / Private clusters. Private customers may require signed images + audit events.

samir: Oncall question — do we have a mitigation we can flip on quickly (config or firewall) if something breaks during rollout?

lena: mitigation plan: (1) patch protobuf -> rebuild images with pinned safe version (3.21.x or patched backport); (2) recompile FlashAttention with vendor patch; (3) bump sentencepiece and add stricter input validation; (4) smoke tests + perf regression tests. If anything fails, route traffic to CPU fallback pool and disable kernel acceleration for affected models.

mike: I can own protobuf rebuild. Quick steps I'm running locally:

```
# in runtime repo
sed -i 's|protobuf==3.20.*|protobuf==3.21.12|' requirements.txt
docker build -t runtime-gpu:patch-1971122334 -f Dockerfile.gpu .
pytest tests/unit --maxfail=1
```
I'll open a PR with the pin + changelog.

tara: I'll validate vLLM behavior with FlashAttention patched and run our long-seq stress harness. If sequence>8192 hits, we need immediate rollback plan.

josh: For Dedicated/Private: packaging notes — images must be signed and uploaded to the private registry. If customers have immutable registries, we'll coordinate with AD to push the new tag and provide SBOM + sig. Also add a note about KMS: rewrapping keys not required for image push, but if we rotate container encryption keys we must coordinate with security.

patch-bot: Created issue ENGSEC-4382 "runtime deps: protobuf/flash/ sentencepiece triage" and assigned to @mike, @tara. Ticket: https://tracker.redwood/ENGSEC-4382

sre-oncall: request: enable extra audit logging for deploys and KMS access during the rollout window. We should capture image pull events + key-access logs to aid postmortem if needed. Cost <-> retention tradeoff acknowledged.

lena: Agreed. josh can you add an audit retention override for the next 72h for deploys? We only need high fidelity during canary & first 48h of prod traffic.

josh: yes I can grant a temporary retention policy for org:inference-deploy for 72h starting when canary begins. Will require a short runbook entry for how to revert.

mike: ETA on PR: 90–120m for a rebuild + unit tests. If green, I'll push a canary tag to staging and ping here.

tara: I'll run perf/regression in parallel — should have results in ~3h. If FlashAttention perf drops >15% we fallback to CPU kernels for critical routes.

samir: I'll stand by to execute rollback plan if canary shows errors. Need a one-liner to flip fallback at runtime?

lena: yes — runtime toggle is `PATCH /admin/config?disable_flashattention=true` in the admin plane. Only ops role can call it (RBAC). Make sure RBAC entries are verified before rollout.

josh: I'll add a short RBAC checklist to ENGSEC-4382: who can trigger fallback, who can rotate KMS, and who can sign images. Also add audit log endpoints to monitor.

mike: pushing canary tag now to staging: runtime-gpu:patch-1971122334-canary — running e2es.

patch-bot: [automated] canary deployment started in staging cluster cluster-stg-2 by mike at 1971122460

tara: e2e smoke passed. Stress harness running.

lena: great — next steps: (A) notify sales/customer success for Private customers with optional opt-in patch window; (B) run Dedicated rollout in small batches; (C) schedule Hosted rollout with incremental ramp and monitoring alerts on error-rate, latencies, and KMS access spikes.

samir: noted. I'll create the rollback page and keep a war-room channel open for the next 12h.

lena: thanks everyone — we'll reconvene in 2h or earlier if anything blows up. Logged owners in ENGSEC-4382. :lock:
